topics.topic: Boundary and precedence between data_provider constants, generated values, and runtime configuration/defaults
questions: Are these values deploy-time configuration with defaults, or fixed product constants owned by `data_provider`?
How is a generated-code value classified when it is also a runtime default, runtime setting, or deterministic-backend IR value?
May Registry timeout, session TTLs, and credential entropy vary by deployment, or are they release constants identical in every environment?
Which moved A30 values remain fields/defaults of `RuntimeSettings`, and which are removed from the runtime-environment table because `data_provider` now owns them?

quotes:
Runtime knobs with confirmed defaults (deployment values may differ):

```text
registry_endpoint_env_name            = REGISTRY_BASE_URL
registry_timeout_seconds               = 5
staff_session_ttl_hours                = 12
viewer_session_ttl_days                = 30
credential_entropy_bytes               = 32
credential_hash_scheme                 = argon2id (library defaults; fixed in source, not a deployment value)
binary_read_limit_env_name             = BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES (required positive integer)
```

`config.*` (SPEC_STANDARD 15.3.1, runtime settings and configuration). Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): the Registry variable name, request paths and timeout, the staff and viewer session lifetimes and the credential entropy have the same value in every environment and change only by a decision about the product, so by SPEC_STANDARD 15.2 (check 4 before 3) they are data-provider constants that generated code imports (`REGISTRY_BASE_URL_VARIABLE`, `REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH`, `REGISTRY_CONTEXT_SEGMENT`, `REGISTRY_VALIDATE_SEGMENT`, `REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `STAFF_SESSION_TTL_HOURS`, `VIEWER_SESSION_TTL_DAYS`, `CREDENTIAL_SECRET_BYTES`), values unchanged; the path templates are split into a path and two segments, because a template is not data (15.11). The Registry URL itself stays an environment value read by the gateway; SOURCE.md records that it is read outside `runtime_settings` (SPEC_STANDARD 6.11), an owner question.
judgement.divergence: One implementation accepts deployment-specific Registry timeouts, session lifetimes and credential entropy, while another always uses the release constants from `data_provider`; deployment operators and authenticated users observe different timeout and expiry behavior.
judgement.why: A30 simultaneously permits deployment-specific values and declares the same values identical in every environment and owned as release constants.
